title: Powerica Ltd - 544744 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Powerica FY26 revenue crossed INR3,012 crore (+13.5% YoY) and EBITDA margin was 12.8%; management targets double-digit FY27 top-line growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR801 crore (+10.9% YoY) with EBITDA of INR86 crore (10.8% margin) and PAT of INR45 crore (5.6% margin). Full-year FY26 PAT of INR277 crore (9.2% margin) was helped by a INR51 crore deferred tax credit from a tax regime change. Management said the IPO-related debt repayment of INR525 crore should cut finance costs from Q1 FY27, and cash including investments was about INR450 crore as of May 26. Management flagged geopolitical tensions, energy prices and supply-chain pressure as weighing on near-term demand, especially in Q1 FY27, and said margin pressure seen in Q4 is temporary.

segments.name: DG Sets (Cummins-powered)
segments.commentary: About 83% of FY26 revenue with 10.9% YoY growth and 9.1% EBITDA margin; Cummins-powered DG sets were about 66% of revenue. Data centers were about 12% of the Cummins business, and high-horsepower sets were over 50% of value.

segments.name: MSLG (medium-speed large generators)
segments.commentary: About 5% of FY26 revenue. Project-driven, with revenue tied to execution milestones and project cycles of 12 to 48 months, so management wants it judged over multiple quarters. The Australia project is 90-95% complete.

segments.name: Allied businesses
segments.commentary: EMI shelters, containers, defence applications, acoustic enclosures, Schneider Electric Prisma panels and project work; about 12.5% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Wind (IPP, EPC, O&M for BoP)
segments.commentary: INR512 crore in FY26 (16.9% of revenue), +28.6% YoY with 31.3% EBITDA margin. IPP is about 40% and EPC/O&M about 60% of wind revenue. Owns 12 Gujarat projects with 330.85 MW installed.

segments.name: Platino Automotive (associate)
segments.commentary: Retrofit emission control device (RECD) for pre-CPCB4+ DG sets of 125 kVA and above, cutting emissions by up to 92%; device cost INR3-30 lakh per installation. FY26 was a marketing-infrastructure build year; Q4 sales INR22 crore and PBT INR5.8 crore.

guidance_outlook: Targeting double-digit top-line growth in FY27.
DG sets organic growth target of about 11-12% in FY27, against an industry growth estimate of about 10.5%.
Management expects margins to recover, with the 50 MW wind capacity contributing from Q2 FY27 and higher wind generation in the first two quarters.
Finance cost to fall substantially from Q1 FY27 after debt repayment, which should lift PAT margin.
Revenue mix expected to move to about 75-80% gensets and 20-25% wind, with the EBITDA mix shifting further toward wind.
Depreciation to rise in FY27 as another 50 MW is capitalised, with about INR400 crore of EPC BoP business expected each year.
capex_capacity: Wind IPP portfolio: 12 Gujarat projects at 330.85 MW installed; a further 52.7 MW project under construction takes it to about 384 MW at completion.
Secured 100 MW of GUVNL bids at Botad, with another 50 MW at advanced planning stage.
Khavda 2 GW RE project with GE Vernova JV is on hold pending land allotment from the Gujarat government.
FY26 capex was 51.3 MW for the business. MSLG needs no capex, as it is a service model.
Manufacturing in Bangalore, Silvassa and Khopoli; everything except the engine and alternator is made in-house.
demand_pricing: Data center demand is strong, with an order book of 9 months to about a year of work and continuing inquiries, which management says rose after the budget.
EPC BoP order book is about 585 MW, including 175 MW in Gujarat (completion expected by Dec 2026) and 410 MW for Torrent Power in Maharashtra; orders run to about Dec 2027.
Wind IPP PPAs are 25-year, fixed-tariff contracts with GUVNL and SECI.
EPC installation work on data centers ranges from 25% to 75% of the supply order value.
Competitive pressure is rising in wind through ROW and land constraints, per management.
Management did not name data center competitors and said it could not quantify the data center share of hyperscaler capex.

qa_highlights.question: What were Platino's Q4 revenue and PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Deferred to a later point in the call; Ritesh Agrawal then said Q4 FY26 Platino sales were INR22 crore with PBT of INR5.8 crore (PAT not given).

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins stay at about 10.5% in FY27 after the softer Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the Q3/Q4 dip temporary, citing geopolitical tensions, and expects FY27 to be in target range. It expects better margins from Q2 onward, helped by the 50 MW wind capacity and higher wind generation in the first two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Are wind EPC/O&M inquiries facing land and connectivity delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradeep Gupta said the order book covers 585 MW to about Dec 2027, so there is enough work in hand. The 175 MW Gujarat project should complete by Dec 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Khavda 2 GW project timeline and the ROW situation?
qa_highlights.answer: The Khavda project is a long-term JV with GE Vernova and is still waiting for land from the Gujarat government. ROW issues are not improving, as competition and RE investment grow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IPP EBITDA margin and PLF?
qa_highlights.answer: The portfolio's EBITDA margin is about 60-62%. New machines run at 36.5% PLF and older ones at 23-24%, with an average of about 26% across the roughly 280 MW profile. New projects earn about 87-88% EBITDA in year one, stabilising at 82-83%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue split between EPC and IPP, and what growth drivers are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: IPP capacity will grow each year as projects are added, while EPC BoP work of about INR400 crore a year (250-300 MW) is steady. Growth drivers cited are data centers, manufacturing, realty, EV charging backup and rental. Over four to five years the revenue mix is expected at about 75:25 gensets to wind.

qa_highlights.question: How does Powerica view competition from fuel-cell technology such as Bloom Energy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would deliver any new technology to market and that gensets stay as backup for 20-25 years. Jai Ram Oberoi said the company is a power solutions provider, not only a DG set maker.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DG set growth outlook, split between price and volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic DG growth target is about 11-12% for FY27, with MSLG contributing on a milestone basis. Management did not split price from volume.

qa_highlights.question: Is Platino expected to grow faster than DG sets?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Jai Ram Oberoi said Platino is a small, high-growth business supported by state-level mandates, and FY26 was spent building marketing infrastructure.

risks_watch: Geopolitical tension, energy prices and supply-chain pressure are expected to weigh on Q1 FY27 demand and margins.
Khavda 2 GW project is held up until the Gujarat government allots land; no timeline was given.
Right-of-way and land constraints in wind are unlikely to ease and are raising competition for sites.
FY26 PAT was helped by a INR51 crore deferred tax credit, so the underlying PAT margin is lower than the reported 9.2%.
Data center exposure is about 12% of revenue; management would not name competitors or quantify the share of hyperscaler capex.
Platino's contribution is small (Q4 sales INR22 crore) and depends on enforcement of state-level RECD mandates.
MSLG revenue is lumpy because it depends on milestones over 12-48 months.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term outlook and the data center order book, but cautious on near-term demand and margins, which management attributed to geopolitical tension. Evasive on data center capex share, competitors and Platino Q4 PAT, and it deferred some answers.
key_quotes: So we target an organic growth of about 11%, 12%.
So this segment should be evaluated from a multi-quarter perspective instead of looking into a particular single quarter.
Because Powerica is not a DG Set manufacturer, we are a power solutions provider.
